parts.title: Look Who Was Talking
parts.article:
(A) When did we start talking to each other and how long did it take us to become so good at it? One view of language development, held by linguists such as Noam Chomsky and anthropologists such as Richard Klein, is that language, specifically the spoken word, appeared suddenly among modern humans a mere 35,000 to 50,000 years ago and that the ability to speak words and use syntax was recently genetically hard-wired into our brains in a kind of language organ. This view of language is associated with the old idea that logical thought is dependent on words, a concept originating with Plato and much in vogue in the 19th century – that is, animals do not speak because they do not think. However, the abstract thought demonstrated in 20th-century experiments with chimpanzees and bonobos put this theory in doubt.

(B) An alternative to the Chomskian theory is that language developed as a series of inventions. This was first suggested by the 18th-century philosopher Etienne Bonnot de Condillac. He argued that spoken language had developed out of gesture language (langage d’action) and that both were inventions arising initially from the simple association between action and object. The theory sees gesture language as arising originally among apes as sounds accompanying gestures, with these sounds gradually becoming coded into ‘words’ as the new skill drove its own evolution. Subsequently, coded words developed into deliberate, complex communication. Evolutionary pressures promoted the development of an anatomy geared to speech – the larynx, vocal muscles and a specific part of the brain immediately next to the part responsible for gestures.

(C) The view that spoken language was ultimately a cultural invention like tool-making, which then drove the biological evolution of the brain and vocal apparatus, seems obvious when you think of the development of different languages. The unique features of a language such as French clearly do not result from any physiological aspect of being French but are the cultural possessions of the French-speaking community. Each language evolves from one generation to the next, constantly adapting itself to cope with the learning biases of each new set of young, immature minds.

(D) Those anthropologists and fossil experts who accept that speech started early still tend to think of language evolution as a gradual 2-million-year process, with our own modern human species (Homo sapiens) way out at the top. A major reason for this is the perception that brain growth among humans was gradual over a similar period. Several recent changes in the fossil evidence, though, bring this into doubt.

(E) The first of these is a re-dating of soil layers from the famous Olduvai Gorge in East Africa, where many key fossil remains have been found. A number of big-brained human species appear to be much older than previously thought, with several specimens dating from over a million years ago. When brain sizes for all available skulls are plotted against time using the revised dates, the result is startling: the bulk of increases in brain size was over by around 1.2 million years ago, with some African human species having brain volumes easily within the modern human range by that time.

(F) So, we have the paradox that over the period when our brain was growing most rapidly, our material cultural development, as measured by stone tools, advanced only marginally; then, over a million years later, when the development of anatomically modern humans finally started to accelerate, artistically and technologically, our brains were actually getting smaller.

(G) The additional piece of evidence that makes this paradox all the more significant is that brain size did not just leap between human species in a direct line of ascent towards ourselves. Over the period from 2.5 to 1.5 million years ago, brains were growing more rapidly than at any time since, within all the different human species. The logical conclusion is that there must have been a unique new behaviour driving brain growth, shared between all species of humans.

(H) So, what was driving rapid brain growth right at the beginning, 2.5 million years ago? The answer may have been staring us in the face. Namely, that not only early humans but their ancestors had started the trend in the very useful skill of verbal communication. Around 2.5 million years ago, the weather took a decided turn for the worse, becoming more variable and colder and drier. The search for food became more taxing, and there would have been a real need to communicate more effectively and cope with the worsening environment in a co-operative way. The near maximum in brain size achieved by 1.2 million years ago indicates that those early ancestors could already have been talking perfectly well. Our brain, which had developed to manipulate and organise complex symbolic aspects of speech internally, could now be turned to a variety of other tasks.

(I) So what happened in the million-year gap after that? Why did we take so long to get to the moon? Cultural evolution aided by communication and teaching is a cumulative interactive process. If each new generation invented just one new skill or idea and passed it on with the rest to their children and cousins, you could predict exactly the same curve of cultural advance as we see from the archaeological and historical record – first very slow, then faster and faster.

Q27

解析 Condillac提出，手势语最早出现在猿类中，随后这种手势语逐渐演变成了人类的口头词汇。

干扰 你可能会看到第3句提到了黑猩猩（chimpanzees），就以为是前面Chomsky的观点，但明确指出语言能追溯到猿类手势的是Condillac。

句子 This was first suggested by the 18th-century philosopher Etienne Bonnot de Condillac. He argued that spoken language had developed out of gesture language (langage d’action) and that both were inventions arising initially from the simple association between action and object. The theory sees gesture language as arising originally among apes as sounds accompanying gestures, with these sounds gradually becoming coded into ‘words’ as the new skill drove its own evolution.

Q28

解析 文章只在第3句提到动物实验被用来反驳旧观念，但Chomsky和Condillac都没有提出过“必须靠动物研究来理解语言发展”。

干扰 你可能会因为文中出现了动物实验就想选A或B，但这只是作者引用的客观事实，并非这两位学者的个人主张。

句子 This view of language is associated with the old idea that logical thought is dependent on words... However, the abstract thought demonstrated in 20th-century experiments with chimpanzees and bonobos put this theory in doubt.

Q29

解析 Chomsky认为语言是在短短3.5万到5万年前才突然出现的，这在动辄几百万年的人类进化史中属于非常晚（relatively late）的时期。

干扰 你可能对数字不敏感，不确定3.5万年前算早还是晚，但对比后文学者提出的200万年进化史，这个时间点毫无疑问就是“相对较晚”。

句子 One view of language development, held by linguists such as Noam Chomsky... is that language, specifically the spoken word, appeared suddenly among modern humans a mere 35,000 to 50,000 years ago...

Q30

解析 Condillac明确主张，口头语言（verbal language）是从手势语（即非口头语言 non-verbal language）中发展而来的。

干扰 你可能没反应过来题目里的“non-verbal language（非口头语言）”其实就是同义替换了原文里的“gesture language（手势语）”。

句子 This was first suggested by the 18th-century philosopher Etienne Bonnot de Condillac. He argued that spoken language had developed out of gesture language...

Q31

解析 语言差异源于文化（环境）而非生理因素的观点出现在第10和11句，但文章并没有说这是Chomsky或Condillac提出的。

干扰 你可能在段落C找到了文化与生理对比的句子就觉得找到了对应，但一定要注意看段落上下文，这里并没有把该观点归功于题目里的任何人。

句子 The view that spoken language was ultimately a cultural invention... seems obvious when you think of the development of different languages. The unique features of a language such as French clearly do not result from any physiological aspect of being French but are the cultural possessions of the French-speaking community.

Q32

解析 第2句指出，Chomsky的语言观与“逻辑思维（理性思考）依赖于词汇（说话）”这一旧观念紧密相连。

干扰 你可能没把原文的“logical thought（逻辑思考）”和题目中的“think rationally（理性思考）”划等号，它们在这里表达的是同一个意思。

句子 One view of language development, held by linguists such as Noam Chomsky... This view of language is associated with the old idea that logical thought is dependent on words...

Q33

解析 有学者认为语言出现在3.5万到5万年前，另一批专家认为是200万年前开始的，说明人类学家们在时间点上根本没有达成一致。

干扰 你可能会漏掉文中明确列出的这两种截然不同的时间线，这种观点的严重分歧直接推翻了题干中的“agree（同意/达成共识）”。

句子 One view of language development... is that language... appeared suddenly among modern humans a mere 35,000 to 50,000 years ago... Those anthropologists and fossil experts who accept that speech started early still tend to think of language evolution as a gradual 2-million-year process...

Q34

解析 原文明确指出这是一个悖论（paradox）：大脑长得最快时技术发展极慢，而技术加速发展时大脑反而变小了，两者并不是直接的正相关。

干扰 你可能会凭直觉认为“脑子越大技术越强”，但原文的“paradox（悖论）”一词和后面的反差对比直接否定了这种想当然的常识。

句子 So, we have the paradox that over the period when our brain was growing most rapidly, our material cultural development, as measured by stone tools, advanced only marginally; then, over a million years later, when the development of anatomically modern humans finally started to accelerate... our brains were actually getting smaller.

Q35

解析 文章第21句确切地给出了大脑生长最快的具体时间段，即250万年前到150万年前之间。

干扰 你可能觉得原文没有原词重现“identified（被确认）”就犹豫不敢选，但既然文章都已经写出了精确的年份区间，就说明这个时期在事实上已经被确认了。

句子 The additional piece of evidence that makes this paradox all the more significant is that brain size did not just leap between human species... Over the period from 2.5 to 1.5 million years ago, brains were growing more rapidly than at any time since...

Q36

解析 全文从头到尾都没有提到过“agriculture（农业）”的发展对语言有任何影响。

干扰 你可能看到文章结尾提到了“cultural advance（文化进步）”就自己脑补了农业的发展，但做阅读题必须严格基于原文，原文没提就是NOT GIVEN。

Q37

解析 原文最后一句清楚地总结了文化发展遵循着一个规律曲线：“一开始非常缓慢，然后越来越快”。

干扰 你可能会觉得“particular pattern（特定模式）”这个词太抽象找不到对应，但它对应的就是原文结尾所描述的那条具体的发展曲线（curve）。

句子 Cultural evolution aided by communication and teaching is a cumulative interactive process. If each new generation invented just one new skill... you could predict exactly the same curve of cultural advance as we see from the archaeological and historical record – first very slow, then faster and faster.

Q38

解析 根据修正后的年代数据（revised dates），大脑体积的绝大部分增长在大概120万年前（1.2 million years ago）就已经完成了。

干扰 题目里的“revised fossil evidence”完美同义替换了原文的“revised dates”，在找年份时不要被其他数字干扰，盯准“revised”去定位就行。

句子 When brain sizes for all available skulls are plotted against time using the revised dates, the result is startling: the bulk of increases in brain size was over by around 1.2 million years ago...

Q39

解析 原文表明，在120万年前大脑达到近乎最大的尺寸，说明早期的祖先在当时已经能够非常流畅地说话了（即语言发展已经完善）。

干扰 你可能会在原文里找“complete（完成）”这个词却找不到，原文说的“talking perfectly well（说得非常好了）”其实就是语言能力发展完善的直白表达。

句子 The near maximum in brain size achieved by 1.2 million years ago indicates that those early ancestors could already have been talking perfectly well.

Q40

解析 在250万年前（2.5 million years ago），气候变差，为了应对恶劣环境，早期人类需要更有效地沟通，这就是影响语言发展的外部变化。

干扰 你可能找不到“external change（外部变化）”，原文说的“weather took a decided turn for the worse（天气变得更糟）”就是迫使人类增加沟通需求的具体外部因素。

句子 Around 2.5 million years ago, the weather took a decided turn for the worse... The search for food became more taxing, and there would have been a real need to communicate more effectively and cope with the worsening environment...
